blocks.text: A pathologist examining a colonic polyp counts dividing cells and finds mitotic figures far from the base of the crypts where division is normally confined. The cells have passed the control points that should have held them back.

blocks.markdown: The **cell cycle** is the ordered sequence by which a cell grows, replicates its DNA and divides. Control matters most in rapidly renewing tissues such as gut epithelium and marrow, where cells must divide only when growth signals are present and DNA is intact. Loss of this control is a defining feature of cancer.

blocks.title: Core definitions
blocks.text: Interphase comprises G1, S and G2; M phase comprises mitosis and cytokinesis. Cells may leave G1 for the quiescent state G0. Cyclins are regulatory proteins whose levels rise and fall through the cycle. Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) are enzymes that phosphorylate target proteins and are active only when bound to a cyclin.

blocks.markdown: **Mitosis.** In prophase chromosomes condense and the spindle forms; in prometaphase the nuclear envelope breaks down and spindle microtubules attach to kinetochores; in metaphase chromosomes align on the metaphase plate; in anaphase sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles; in telophase nuclear envelopes re-form and chromosomes decondense. Cytokinesis, the division of cytoplasm, begins in late anaphase and finishes after telophase.

blocks.markdown: **The G1/S checkpoint mechanism.** In G1 the protein **Rb** (retinoblastoma protein) binds the transcription factor **E2F** and keeps it inactive. Growth factors induce **cyclin D**, which activates **CDK4 and CDK6**; cyclin D-CDK4/6 phosphorylates Rb. Cyclin E then rises and **cyclin E-CDK2** phosphorylates Rb further. Hyperphosphorylated Rb releases E2F, which switches on genes needed for S phase, including cyclin E and DNA replication enzymes. Later cyclins keep the cycle moving: cyclin A-CDK2 in S phase and cyclin B-CDK1 to enter mitosis.

**p53 and DNA damage.** DNA damage activates kinases that stabilise **p53**, which is normally kept low by its inhibitor MDM2. Stabilised p53 acts as a transcription factor and switches on the gene for **p21**, a CDK inhibitor that blocks cyclin E-CDK2. Rb then stays unphosphorylated and E2F stays bound, so the cell halts in G1 and repairs its DNA. If damage is irreparable, p53 instead induces apoptosis.

blocks.title: Cell with DNA damage before S phase
blocks.prompt: A cell has growth factors but sustains DNA damage in G1. Explain the sequence that halts it.

steps.text: Damage signalling stabilises p53, which escapes MDM2-mediated degradation.
p53 induces transcription of p21, a CDK inhibitor.
p21 inhibits cyclin E-CDK2, so Rb is not hyperphosphorylated and keeps E2F bound.
Without free E2F, S-phase genes are not switched on and the cell arrests in G1 until repair is done, or undergoes apoptosis if it cannot be repaired.

blocks.answer: p53 raises p21, which blocks cyclin E-CDK2, keeping Rb-E2F intact and holding the cell in G1.

blocks.title: Estimating the duration of a phase
blocks.prompt: In a steadily growing population with a 20-hour cell cycle, 5% of cells are in mitosis on a section. Estimate how long mitosis lasts.

steps.text: In an asynchronous steady-state population, the fraction of cells in a phase approximates the duration of that phase divided by the total cycle time.
Duration = fraction x cycle time = 0.05 x 20 h = 1 h.

blocks.title: How loss of Rb or p53 drives proliferation
blocks.text: Loss of Rb (as in retinoblastoma) leaves E2F constantly free, so cells enter S phase without proper growth signals. Loss of p53 (as in Li-Fraumeni syndrome and many sporadic cancers) removes p21-mediated arrest and apoptosis, so cells with damaged DNA keep dividing and accumulate mutations. Cancer needs more than one such hit, but both lesions disable the G1/S brake.

items: Cyclin levels oscillate; CDK levels are comparatively steady but need cyclin for activity.
Cyclin D-CDK4/6 and cyclin E-CDK2 drive G1/S by phosphorylating Rb.
p21 (induced by p53) inhibits CDKs; Rb and p53 act as brakes, cyclin-CDK as accelerators.

blocks.title: Do not call cancer simply fast growth
blocks.text: Tumour cells are defined by loss of control: they pass checkpoints inappropriately, not necessarily because the cycle itself is faster.

points: The cycle runs G1, S, G2, M with G0 as a resting state; mitosis proceeds prophase, prometaphase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase.
At G1/S, cyclin D-CDK4/6 and cyclin E-CDK2 phosphorylate Rb, releasing E2F to activate S-phase genes.
p53 induces p21 to block CDKs or triggers apoptosis; loss of Rb or p53 removes these brakes and favours uncontrolled proliferation.

questions.stem: A flow cytometry profile shows a cell population with twice the DNA content of a resting diploid G0 cell, yet the nuclear envelope is still intact. Which phase are these cells in?

options.text: G2
G1
G0
Telophase daughter cells

distractorRationale.a: Correct: 4C DNA with intact nuclear envelope.
distractorRationale.d: Daughter cells after telophase have 2C DNA each.

questions.explanation: DNA doubles during S phase, so cells with 4C DNA are in G2 or early M. An intact nuclear envelope excludes mitosis beyond prophase.

questions.stem: In a squash preparation of root-like proliferating tissue, a cell shows two identical sets of chromosomes at opposite poles with nuclear envelopes beginning to re-form and a cleavage furrow. Which phase is this?

options.text: Telophase
Metaphase
Prophase
Anaphase

distractorRationale.b: Metaphase has chromosomes on the plate.
distractorRationale.c: Prophase has condensing chromosomes and an intact nucleus.
distractorRationale.d: Anaphase is chromatid movement, before envelopes re-form.

questions.explanation: Chromosome sets at opposite poles with envelopes re-forming mark telophase. Cytokinesis is under way as the furrow deepens.

questions.stem: Which sequence correctly describes how growth factors drive a cell past the G1/S checkpoint?

options.text: Cyclin D-CDK4/6 and then cyclin E-CDK2 phosphorylate Rb, releasing E2F to activate S-phase genes
Cyclin B-CDK1 phosphorylates E2F, which then binds and activates Rb
Cyclin D-CDK4/6 phosphorylates p21, which then replicates DNA
Cyclin E-CDK2 binds p53, which releases Rb into the nucleus

questions.correctOptionText: Cyclin D-CDK4/6 and then cyclin E-CDK2 phosphorylate Rb, releasing E2F to activate S-phase genes

distractorRationale.b: Cyclin B-CDK1 acts at G2/M, and E2F is the activator not the target in this way.
distractorRationale.c: p21 is a CDK inhibitor and does not replicate DNA.

questions.explanation: Phosphorylation of Rb by cyclin D-CDK4/6 and cyclin E-CDK2 frees E2F, which drives transcription of S-phase genes. Cyclin B-CDK1 belongs to the G2/M transition.

questions.stem: In an asynchronous, steady-state culture of epithelial cells with a cell cycle of 24 hours, a count of 500 cells finds 20 in mitosis. Estimate the duration of mitosis in hours.
questions.explanation: The mitotic fraction is 20/500 = 0.04. In steady state, phase duration is approximately fraction x cycle length, so 0.04 x 24 = 0.96 hours (about 58 minutes).

questions.stem: Describe the events of mitosis from prophase to telophase and state the key event in each phase.
markingGuide: Prophase: chromosome condensation and spindle formation.
Prometaphase: nuclear envelope breakdown and kinetochore attachment.
Metaphase: alignment at the metaphase plate.
Anaphase: sister chromatid separation and movement to the poles.
Telophase: nuclear envelopes re-form; cytokinesis divides the cytoplasm.
questions.explanation: A good answer gives the phases in order with the defining event of each. Molecular detail is not required.

questions.stem: Ultraviolet damage in a skin keratinocyte stabilises p53. Which immediate downstream event explains the resulting G1 arrest?

options.text: p53 induces p21, which inhibits cyclin E-CDK2 so Rb stays unphosphorylated
p53 phosphorylates Rb directly, releasing E2F
p53 activates cyclin D, which accelerates S phase entry
p53 degrades the spindle so mitosis cannot start

questions.correctOptionText: p53 induces p21, which inhibits cyclin E-CDK2 so Rb stays unphosphorylated

distractorRationale.b: Phosphorylated Rb would release E2F and promote S phase, the opposite of arrest.
distractorRationale.c: p53 does not activate cyclin D to promote S entry.
distractorRationale.d: p53 acts at the checkpoint, not by destroying the spindle.

questions.explanation: p53 acts as a transcription factor for p21, a CDK inhibitor. Blocking cyclin E-CDK2 keeps Rb bound to E2F and halts the cell in G1 for repair.

questions.stem: A diploid G1 cell contains 6.4 picograms of nuclear DNA. How much nuclear DNA, in picograms, does one cell contain in G2, before mitosis?
questions.explanation: S phase replicates the entire genome, so a G2 cell has twice the G1 DNA: 2 x 6.4 = 12.8 picograms. Each daughter cell returns to 6.4 picograms after cytokinesis.

questions.stem: Explain how loss of p53 function contributes to cancer, referring to p21, apoptosis and the fate of damaged cells.
markingGuide: p53 is normally stabilised by DNA damage and acts as a transcription factor.
It induces p21, which inhibits cyclin-CDK activity and arrests cells in G1 for repair.
It induces apoptosis when damage is irreparable.
Without p53, damaged cells do not arrest or die, and continue to replicate DNA and divide.
questions.explanation: The answer must link the normal p53-p21 arrest and apoptosis functions to the consequence of losing them. Persistence of damaged cells drives tumour development.

questions.stem: A child has bilateral retinal tumours in which both copies of the gene for the protein that binds E2F are inactivated. What is the direct cellular consequence?

options.text: E2F is free to activate S-phase genes regardless of growth signals
Cells cannot replicate DNA at all
p21 is permanently overproduced, arresting cells in G1
Cyclin D can no longer be produced

questions.correctOptionText: E2F is free to activate S-phase genes regardless of growth signals

distractorRationale.a: Correct: loss of Rb removes the brake on E2F.
distractorRationale.b: Loss of Rb promotes, not prevents, S entry.
distractorRationale.c: p21 is not the consequence of Rb loss.
distractorRationale.d: Cyclin production is not directly blocked.

questions.explanation: The protein that binds E2F is Rb, so its loss leaves E2F permanently available. Cells then enter S phase without proper mitogenic signals, as in retinoblastoma.

questions.stem: Compare the roles of cyclin-CDK complexes, Rb and p53 in controlling the G1/S transition, and state which behave as accelerators and which as brakes.
markingGuide: Cyclin D-CDK4/6 and cyclin E-CDK2 are accelerators that phosphorylate Rb.
Rb binds E2F; phosphorylation releases E2F to activate S-phase genes, so Rb is a brake.
p53 induces p21, a CDK inhibitor, and apoptosis, so it is a brake responding to DNA damage.
Clear distinction of accelerators versus brakes.
questions.explanation: The two brakes act at different points: Rb restrains E2F, while p53 restrains CDK activity through p21. Cyclin-CDK complexes provide the forward drive.
